'''Eid Hourany''' (18 March 1940 – 17 November 2008) was a French and Lebanese [[nuclear physicist]]. He studied in the Science Faculty in the Lebanese University ({{langx|ar|كلية العلوم، الجامعة اللبنانية}})  at [[Hadath]], [[Beirut]]. He achieved his State PhD in France at the Institut of Nuclear Physics ({{langx|fr|Institut de Physique Nucléaire d'Orsay}}) at [[Orsay]] where he was coached by Dr [[Toshiko Yuasa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum Diaries |url=http://www.quantumdiaries.org/2013/01/18/toshiko-yuasa-la-marie-curie-japonaise-1909-1980/ |access-date=2024-06-07 |website=www.quantumdiaries.org}}</ref> From 1971 until 1982, he was Professor in Physics and finally Head of the Physics department at Hadath University (Beyrouth). He joined the French National Research Centre (CNRS) in 1982. From 1982 until 2006 he pursued several research activities and contributed to more than 80 scientific publications. He officially retired from [[CNRS]] in 2006 with the grade of "Directeur de Recherche".<ref>[http://ipnweb.in2p3.fr/communication/communication/rapport/rapipno200607/annexes/Staff.pdf Rapport 2006/07 de l'IN2P3, Staff list (annex)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216004447/http://ipnweb.in2p3.fr/communication/communication/rapport/rapipno200607/annexes/Staff.pdf|date=2013-12-16}}</ref> He continued his research activity until 2008 (year of death)

==Family==
Eid Hourany was born in [[Yaroun]] (South Lebanon) in March 1940. His parents were Lotof and Jamila Hourany. He had two sisters and two brothers. Due to hazardous translation from Arabic in his early French administrative papers, his name was sometimes referred to as "Hourani" instead of "Hourany".

==Research==
He carried out his first research work during his PhD.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hourany | first1 = E. | year = 1971 | title = Correction geometrique des coefficients de correlation angulaire | journal = Nuclear Instruments and Methods | volume = 94 | issue = 3| pages = 401–412 | doi=10.1016/0029-554X(71)90002-4| bibcode = 1971NucIM..94..401H }}</ref> From 1992 until 1995 he made major contributions to discoveries in [[Cluster decay]] by achieving experimental confirmation of a fine structure in 14C radioactivity of 223Ra.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hourany | first1 = E. | display-authors = etal | year = 1995 | title = 223Ra Nuclear Spectroscopy in 14C Radioactivity | url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/321541/files/PhysRevC.52.267.pdf | journal = Phys. Rev. | volume = 52 | issue = 1| pages = 267–270 | doi=10.1103/physrevc.52.267| pmid = 9970505 | bibcode = 1995PhRvC..52..267H }}</ref> He used for this purpose intense radioactive sources created in [[CERN]] accelerator (Genève) and a superconducting magnetic solenoid developed some years before(named "SOLENO").<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hourani | first1 = E. | last2 = Kumpulainen | first2 = J. | last3 = Azaiez | first3 = F. | last4 = Fortier | first4 = S. | last5 = Gales | first5 = S. | last6 = Maison | first6 = J. M. | last7 = Massolo | first7 = P. | last8 = Ramstein | first8 = B. | last9 = Schapira | first9 = J. P. | year = 1988| title = Mass identification in heavy ion collection with the spectrometer SOLENO | journal = Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A | volume = 264 | issue = 2–3| pages = 357–366 | bibcode=1988NIMPA.264..357H | doi=10.1016/0168-9002(88)90924-2}}</ref> His latest research activity concerned GRAAL European project<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.slideworld.org/slideshow.aspx/HIV/viewslides.aspx/nstar2009.ihep.ac.cn-B326-20-Vegna%20NSTAR%202009.ppt-ppt-2266363 | title=Nstar2009.ihep.ac.cn/B326/20/Vegna20NSTAR202009.PPT Powerpoint Presentation}}</ref><ref>Latest results from GRAAL collaboration
V. Vegna et al 2009 Chinese Phys. C 33 1249 doi:10.1088/1674-1137/33/12/032 http://iopscience.iop.org/1674-1137/33/12/032</ref>(to be documented).

==Lebanese University, Science Faculty==
He studied physics in the Lebanese University before gaining a scholarship to specialise in nuclear physics in France. From 1971 and after completing his PhD, he taught in the Faculty of Science in the Lebanese University and became the Head of the Physics Department until 1982.<ref name="National Council of Scientific Research Lebanon">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnrs.edu.lb/info/nachra/NashraNo138.pdf|title=وفاة الفيزيائي النووي حوراني في فرنسا page 15|access-date=2010-03-17|publisher=National Council of Scientific Research Lebanon|language=Arabic}}</ref>
